game: GB @ DET, Week 7 2026, morning of kickoff (pack only; weeks < 7)

script.base: DET is home -4 in a 55.5 game (implied DET 29.8, GB 25.8), so the book expects a competitive high-scoring game, not a blowout. Detroit still features Jahmyr Gibbs on the ground (60 carries, 296 rush yards in weeks 3-5, about 20 carries and 99 rush yards a game) while Jared Goff feeds Amon-Ra St. Brown (30 targets), Sam LaPorta (22 targets, 216 yards) and Jameson Williams (16 targets, 198 yards, 302 air). Green Bay, a 4-point dog, throws: Matthew Golden is the target leader (27 targets, 248 yards, 401 air in weeks 4-6), Christian Watson is the other vertical (19/254/347), Tucker Kraft is the short piece (20/143/61). Both implied totals clear 25, so pass volume stays live on both sides and Gibbs still gets the late lead-back carries if DET is in front.
script.flip1: DET jumps up by two scores early and clocks it with Gibbs (his last-4 rush line includes a 151). GB abandons the run, so Marshawn Lloyd (25/54 in the L3 window, 2.16 YPC), K. Johnson (16/66) and Pierre Strong (16/35) rush lines die, while Golden, Watson and Kraft targets rise in catch-up. DET pass-catcher snaps can stall late if the script becomes Gibbs-only.
script.flip2: GB hangs or leads, so Goff (already +0.41 EPA/db when blitzed, and GB blitzes 34%) airs it out and LaPorta/Williams/St. Brown volume rises while Gibbs rush unders live. The other flip is an unpriced weather slog: forecast is not in the pack, and wind 15+ or rain would cut Golden/Watson deep yards and drag a 55.5 total under.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, man/zone rate, or MOFO/MOFC in the pack. Location proxy only: DET allows 10.98 YPA in the middle (43 attempts) versus 5.78 left (72) and 7.49 right (96). GB is compact: 6.56 left (72), 6.09 middle (47), 5.46 right (91).
matchup.pressure: DET blitzes 29%. GB EPA/db is -0.04 when blitzed versus +0.20 when not, so pressure hurts Jordan Love and would cut Golden/Watson deep yards while boosting Kraft and RB checkdowns. GB blitzes 34%. DET EPA/db is +0.41 when blitzed versus +0.22 when not, so Goff is better against pressure and the TE/RB answers (LaPorta, Gibbs receiving) stay live.
matchup.bleeds: DET's bleed is the middle (10.98 YPA) plus explosives: 23 passes of 20+ in 5 games (listed 23/231) versus GB's 9 in 6 games (9/225). DET also allows 4.48 rush YPC and 17 runs of 10+ in 5 games. GB allows 4.14 rush YPC and 14 runs of 10+ in 6 games, with no location hole above 6.56 YPA.
matchup.overlap: GB's target leader is Golden, but at 401 air yards on 27 targets (about 14.9 air/target) he attacks DET's explosive leak, not the 10.98 middle. The player who actually attacks that middle is Kraft (20 targets, only 61 air yards), and his yards have not cleared 51.5. On the other side the clean overlap is LaPorta (22 targets, 216 yards, 202 air in the L3 window) into a GB defense missing LB Franklin, against a team that blitzes 34% and that Goff has beaten.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. LaPorta lost because GB's pass defense traveled (6.09 middle YPA, only 9 explosives in six games), a backup linebacker plus a safety bracket took the TE away, Goff's blitz-beater throws went to Gibbs and St. Brown instead, and a moderate DET lead let Gibbs (60 carries in three games) salt it so LaPorta finished on the 44-yard side of 49.5. Golden lost because the 21-yard floor is real, DET's left side at 5.78 YPA can erase an outside vertical, Aaron Banks was limited and even a 29% blitz was enough given GB's -0.04 EPA when pressured, and either GB led and ran or unpriced wind killed the 401 air yards before they became 73.5 receiving yards. That counter is real, which is why Golden is a lean and not a strong, but it is not stronger than the base read: the cushion on both numbers is double-digit yards and the prices are still pick'ems.
slip_story: One story only: a 55.5 competitive shootout lean, DET -4, both teams throwing. LaPorta over is the DET intermediate piece with Franklin out and GB blitzing 34%. Golden over is the GB dog pass-volume piece into DET's explosive leak. They win together in the base script and in a mild DET lead. Do not add a game under, a Gibbs rush-only clock-kill under, or a Kraft under. No touchdowns, one market per player, two legs, main rungs only. Gibbs receiving over 41.5 would be the correlated third if a human wants the full Franklin-out stack, but it is not one of the two edges here because the cushion (about 48-51 versus 41.5) is thinner.
